claim: A cash score of 100 needs market growth above 30% a year
meaning: Usually true, not always: very cheap compute or favorable costs together can bring the threshold below 30%.

claim: The same, with compute at 6% of revenue
meaning: Below 30% only when tax, the accountability floor and AI failure costs are all near their favorable ends.

claim: The threshold stays above 30% in 2028, 2031 and 2036
meaning: As for the first row: it depends on the compute path.

claim: Passing savings to customers raises every threshold
meaning: Not where compute costs nearly as much as the labor it replaces; there full automation costs more than today.

claim: No Rule of 100 on the central path by 2036
meaning: Holds in every world tested: the best score found is below 100.

claim: Even a completed program stays below 100 in 2036
meaning: Crosses 100 only at the top of market growth with the most favorable costs.

claim: Less than half the program realized by 2036
meaning: True at the central pace; a firm that changes faster can realize much more.

claim: The program is still running in 2036
meaning: Fast execution can finish before 2036, as the paper's fast case does.

claim: The central path rises from 2028 to 2036
meaning: Can dip between horizons if frontier-only work grows over time.

claim: The central path lies between its two spend-basis bounds
Yearly gains overtake transition costs before payback

meaning: Fast execution or favorable compute paths can pay back sooner.

conditions: Central execution, fixed prices, no capital
meaning: Below five years only on compute paths that start high and fall steeply.

claim: Lifetime gains are worth more than the transition costs
meaning: Slow execution can leave the gains below the costs, as the paper's slow case does.

conditions: Central execution, fixed prices, no capital

claim: A Rule of 1000 is not a steady state
The growth engine beats the back-office cut at one of six positions
meaning: Zero or one position, depending on the maintenance level of selling spend; the back office leads elsewhere.

claim: No AI-only control design on one provider passes
meaning: Holds in every world tested: shared failures of one model never fall far enough.
